pages.title: Tests
pages.content:
Tests

Tests

We provide mechanical and chemical testing for concrete, steel reinforcement, core samples, and aggregates. Every test is conducted to recognised standard methods with EN or ASTM equivalents named on the report.

Compressive Strength Testing

Compressive strength testing determines the maximum axial load concrete can sustain prior to structural failure. We test sets of 3 cylinders measuring either 100 by 200 millimetres or 150 by 300 millimetres. The test procedures adhere to recognised standard methods, with EN and ASTM equivalents named directly on your report. Testing establishes structural compliance against designated design mixes. Standard turnaround is 2 working days following the designated test date, with an express 24-hour service available for a 40 percent surcharge. The fee is $85 per set of 3 cylinders.

Flexural Strength Testing

Flexural strength tests evaluate the tensile bending resistance of unreinforced concrete beams subjected to third-point or center-point loading. Specimens are standard cast beams prepared during placement. The method complies with recognised standard methods, and all EN or ASTM equivalent procedures are cited on the signed PDF report. This testing reveals load-bearing capacity and modulus of rupture for pavements and slabs. Turnaround is 2 working days, or 24 hours under our express option with a 40 percent fee uplift. The charge is $70 per beam.

Slump and Air Content Verification

Fresh concrete workability and entrained air volume are assessed directly on site during placement. Our site technicians record slump cone displacement and measure air void ratios across batch deliveries. All testing conforms to recognised standard methods, listing EN and ASTM equivalents on the completed report. These checks verify consistency before batch placement proceeds across the structure. The fee is $140 per site visit covering up to 6 tests. Reports are issued within 2 working days of testing, or within 24 hours at a 40 percent express rate.

Rebar Tensile and Bend Testing

Tensile and bend testing establishes the yield point, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation properties of reinforcing steel bars. Individual bars are clamped in precision mechanical grips and pulled to fracture, followed by mandrel cold bend tests. Testing follows recognised standard methods, with all relevant EN and ASTM equivalents specified on the final report. These tests ensure the steel reinforcement meets structural ductility requirements. Standard turnaround is 2 working days from intake, with 24-hour express available at a 40 percent surcharge. The fee is $60 per bar.

Core Extraction and Testing

Concrete core testing assesses in-situ strength in hardened structural elements. Extracted cylindrical cores must feature a diameter at least 3 times the nominal aggregate size. Following diamond drilling, cores are trimmed, measured, moisture conditioned, and crushed in the compression frame. All steps follow recognised standard methods, citing EN and ASTM equivalents on the signed report. Results provide accurate confirmation of existing member integrity. Turnaround is 2 working days, or 24 hours under our 40 percent express rate. The fee is $165 per core.

Density and Absorption Assessment

Density and water absorption measurements indicate void structure, permeability, and compaction quality of hardened concrete specimens. Technicians measure dry mass, saturated surface-dry mass, and buoyant mass using hydro-static balances. Procedures follow recognised standard methods, with EN and ASTM equivalent designations detailed in the certified report. These parameters help engineers assess durability and potential environmental degradation over time. The fee is $45 per specimen. Standard report delivery takes 2 working days, with 24-hour express reporting available for a 40 percent surcharge.

Chloride Content Analysis

Chemical chloride analysis identifies chloride ion penetration in concrete, which poses corrosion risks to embedded reinforcement. Powdered sample increments extracted from specified structural depths are analyzed in the chemistry lab. Testing follows recognised standard methods, and equivalent EN and ASTM procedures are fully referenced on the report. This analysis maps chloride profiles to inform durability modeling and cathodic protection planning. Turnaround is 2 working days, or 24 hours under our 40 percent express rate. The cost is $95 per sample.

Custom Test Plans

When structural projects involve non-standard load configurations, specialized curing regimes, or unique sample geometries, we establish custom laboratory protocols. Custom test plans are formulated to recognized standard methods, referencing appropriate EN and ASTM equivalents on all documentation. Our technical leads review project specifications to structure a tailored testing regime. Turnaround is typically 2 working days from completion of testing, with 24-hour express options carrying a 40 percent surcharge. Project-specific plans start from $250 depending on scope.

How to send

How to Send a Sample

Submitting material samples to Kensa Laboratory follows four simple steps from online booking to final reporting. We accept drop-offs during receiving hours or coordinate courier collections to ensure samples arrive in sound condition.

1

Book Your Submission Online

Every sample intake begins with our online submission booking form. You provide your contact details, company name, site project reference, required testing types, specimen count, and the concrete cast date. Once submitted, our system immediately emails your official submission number. This submission number links your material to your job file and secures space on our laboratory testing schedule upon arrival. Booking ahead ensures our technicians prepare curing tanks, test platens, and analytical equipment in advance of your delivery date.

2

Label and Pack Your Specimens

Each specimen must be clearly marked with its assigned submission number and cast date using a waterproof marker directly on the specimen surface. Concrete test cylinders must be either 100 by 200 millimetres or 150 by 300 millimetres. Extracted core samples must have a core diameter at least 3 times the nominal aggregate size. Protect specimens from impact, moisture loss, and extreme temperatures during transit. Pack cylinders and cores upright in sturdy crates or insulated boxes with adequate cushioning.

3

Drop Off or Courier Delivery

Deliver your prepared specimens to our laboratory receiving bay at Unit 4, 18 Harbour Works Road, Northgate. Sample receiving is open Monday through Friday from 08:30 to 16:00. Saturday drop-offs between 09:00 and 12:00 are available strictly by prior arrangement. We are closed Sundays and public holidays. Alternatively, you may arrange a dedicated courier delivery to our receiving counter. Our reception team logs each consignment within the hour of arrival to maintain clear custody tracking.

4

Testing and Report Issuance

On the scheduled test date, our technicians retrieve specimens from curing tanks or preparation racks and perform testing in accordance with recognised standard methods. We issue a formal, signed PDF test report within 2 working days following test completion. If your project faces urgent deadlines, our express testing option delivers reports within 24 hours for a 40 percent fee uplift. Tested physical specimens are retained in our storage facility for 30 days following report distribution.

pages.title: Fees
pages.content:
Fees

Testing Fees

Kensa Laboratory maintains transparent, flat pricing across all routine materials testing services. Our published fee schedule outlines standard testing rates, turnaround options, and payment terms.

Flat unit prices. No surprises on the invoice.

Standard Laboratory Test Pricing

Our laboratory charges fixed unit prices for routine testing services. Compressive strength testing is $85 per set of 3 cylinders. Flexural strength testing is $70 per beam. On-site slump and air content testing is $140 per site visit, which includes up to 6 separate tests. Rebar tensile and bend testing is $60 per bar. Concrete core extraction and testing is $165 per core. Density and absorption assessment is $45 per specimen. Chemical chloride content analysis is $95 per sample. For non-standard investigations, a custom test plan starts from $250 per project.

Express Turnaround and Additional Services

Standard written reports are issued as signed PDFs within 2 working days following test execution. When immediate verification is required for site decisions, we provide an express 24-hour turnaround service with a 40 percent surcharge applied to the base testing fee. On-site attendance fees cover standard site visits for testing and coring within our service area. Additional signed copies of formal test reports can be requested at any time while specimens remain within their 30-day post-report retention period.

Invoicing and Payment Terms

Invoices are generated following the distribution of final test reports and reference your project name and submission number. Payment terms are strictly 30 days from the invoice date. We accept direct bank transfers and standard commercial payment methods. Accounts must remain current to schedule ongoing testing or receive express report prioritisation. For high-volume projects or continuous sampling contracts, customized billing schedules can be arranged in coordination with our administrative office.

Prices above are the same on every page of this site.

Lab & People

Founded in 2009, Kensa Laboratory delivers impartial material evaluation and mechanical testing for construction projects. In 2017, we expanded operations by relocating to our dedicated testing facility at Harbour Works.

Laboratory History and Testing Facility

Kensa Laboratory was established in 2009 to provide independent, reliable materials verification for regional engineering works. To support growing testing volumes and larger mechanical testing frames, the lab moved to Unit 4, 18 Harbour Works Road, Northgate in 2017. Our facility houses climate-controlled curing tanks, precision compression machines, high-capacity rebar tensile frames, and dedicated wet chemistry benches. Operating as an impartial third party, we deliver verifiable material data to help engineers, contractors, and project owners make grounded decisions.

Case notes

Case Notes

Our case notes document recent materials testing programs across civil infrastructure, institutional buildings, and commercial retrofits. These summaries highlight how methodical testing verifies structural safety and resolves site uncertainty.

Sampling dates

Pedestrian Bridge Deck Pour

For a municipal pedestrian bridge deck pour, Kensa Laboratory conducted compressive strength verification on sets of 3 concrete cylinders at 7-day and 28-day curing intervals, alongside hardened core extraction testing. Cylinders measuring 100 by 200 millimetres were stored in temperature-controlled curing tanks prior to compression loading. Test results confirmed that the placed concrete exceeded specified design strength thresholds across all deck spans. Hardened cores confirmed uniform compaction and aggregate distribution throughout the suspended slab, allowing falsework striking to proceed on schedule.

Primary School Extension

During construction of a primary school extension, our field and bench teams provided integrated fresh concrete and reinforcement verification. Technicians attended site placements to execute slump and air content tests, ensuring batch consistency across foundation pours. Simultaneously, our metals laboratory performed tensile and bend tests on reinforcing steel bar samples taken directly from site deliveries. The resulting test data verified that both the concrete matrix and rebar yield properties satisfied required structural ductility and load-bearing design specifications.

Mid-Rise Commercial Retrofit

A mid-rise commercial retrofit project required comprehensive structural evaluation of existing load-bearing concrete shear walls prior to vertical alterations. Marcus Lindqvist oversaw diamond core drilling on site, extracting cores with diameters exceeding 3 times the aggregate size. Back in our laboratory, the team executed compression crushing alongside chemical chloride content profiling across depth increments directed by Priya Nair. The findings identified sound core strength and minimal chloride intrusion, enabling project structural engineers to approve the proposed retrofit design without costly member replacements.

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

Find clear answers to common questions about submitting samples, test methods, pricing, and report delivery. If your project has requirements not covered here, contact our technical team directly.

Sending

How do I prepare and label specimens before sending them?

Each specimen must be clearly labeled with its assigned submission number and cast date using a waterproof marker directly on the concrete or steel. For concrete compression, standard cylinder sizes are 100 by 200 millimetres or 150 by 300 millimetres. For extracted core specimens, the core diameter must be at least 3 times the nominal aggregate size. Secure specimens in sturdy, cushioned crates or containers to prevent physical damage or moisture loss during transport to our laboratory receiving bay.

What are your receiving hours and drop-off procedures?

Sample receiving is open Monday through Friday from 08:30 to 16:00 at Unit 4, 18 Harbour Works Road, Northgate. Saturday intake from 09:00 to 12:00 is available strictly by prior arrangement. We are closed Sundays and public holidays. You may deliver specimens personally, send a representative, or arrange courier dispatch. Our sample reception lead, Lena Hoffmann, logs every arriving consignment within one hour of arrival to confirm condition and verify test scheduling against your online booking.

How big should a cylinder or a core be?

Cylinders are 100 by 200 or 150 by 300. A core should be at least three times the aggregate size. If a specimen falls outside that, tell us in the booking before you send it.

What do I write on the specimen?

Write the submission number and the cast date on each specimen. Keep any other mark illegible. We match the label to the booking at receiving, not from a photograph.

Results

When will I receive my formal test report?

Standard written reports are issued as signed PDF documents within 2 working days following the scheduled test date. Reports detail all recorded measurements, fracture modes, and relevant standard method citations, including EN and ASTM equivalent procedures. For urgent projects, we provide an express testing option that delivers signed reports within 24 hours of test completion for a 40 percent surcharge. Once reported, physical specimens are stored in our laboratory archive for 30 days before disposal.

How long do you keep the sample?

Thirty days after the report. After that the specimen is released. Collect it inside that window if you need it back.

Are you accredited, or do you endorse a pour?

No. Kensa Laboratory does not claim accreditation, awards or site endorsements. The report states what the specimen did under the test you booked, written to recognised standard methods, with the EN or ASTM equivalent named on the report.

Fees

How are fees calculated and what are your payment terms?

We charge flat unit rates per test: $85 per set of 3 compression cylinders, $70 per flexural beam, $140 per site visit for slump and air testing up to 6 tests, $60 per rebar tensile bar, $165 per core extraction and test, $45 per density specimen, $95 per chloride sample, and custom test plans from $250. Payment terms are 30 days from invoice issuance. Invoices reference your project name and submission number for straightforward accounting reconciliation.

Site visits

Do you come to site?

Slump and air content is a site visit, up to six tests, at $140. Core extraction is booked per core at $165 and includes the drilling. Other tests are run on specimens you deliver or that a courier brings to the bay.

Still unsure about a specimen? Say so in the booking.

Book a submission

Book a Submission

Book your laboratory testing submission before dropping off specimens or scheduling courier delivery. Booking in advance reserves space in our curing tanks and secures your target testing date.

Online Submission Booking Form

To initiate testing, complete our online booking form prior to specimen dispatch. The form captures your contact name, company details, site project reference, required testing categories, total specimen count, specimen cast date, and intended drop-off date. Upon submission, an automated confirmation emails your dedicated submission number. Writing this submission number clearly on all specimens ensures instant intake matching when your consignment reaches Lena Hoffmann at our receiving bay at Unit 4, 18 Harbour Works Road, Northgate.

Receiving Hours and Facility Directions

Our receiving bay operates Monday through Friday between 08:30 and 16:00, with Saturday morning drop-offs from 09:00 to 12:00 by arrangement. General laboratory hours are Monday through Friday from 08:00 to 17:30. We are closed on Sundays and public holidays. We are located at Unit 4, 18 Harbour Works Road, Northgate, accessible via commercial vehicle routes with dedicated loading spaces directly outside the receiving bay doors for easy offloading of crates and coolers.

Unit 4, 18 Harbour Works Road, Northgate. Receiving Mon–Fri 08:30–16:00. Lab Mon–Fri 08:00–17:30.

Courier Collection and Site Assistance

If site personnel cannot deliver specimens directly, you can coordinate courier transport directly to our Northgate receiving bay or request assistance with sample collection logistics. When dispatching via courier, ensure transit packaging protects against impact and moisture evaporation. For projects requiring on-site fresh testing or diamond core drilling, Marcus Lindqvist coordinates field visits for slump, air content, and core extraction. Our team ensures chain-of-custody documentation is established from initial collection through laboratory analysis.

pages.title: Terms of testing
pages.content:
Terms

Terms of Testing

These terms govern all materials testing, core extraction, site visits, and analytical reporting provided by Kensa Laboratory. Engaging our services constitutes acceptance of these standard testing conditions.

Sample Retention and Disposal

Kensa Laboratory retains all tested physical specimens for exactly 30 days following the issuance of the final signed test report. During this 30-day retention period, clients may request additional report copies or re-examination where feasible. Once the 30-day period elapses, specimens are safely disposed of according to standard environmental procedures unless written instructions requesting extended storage are agreed upon in advance. Unused sample portions or hazardous chemical residues will be managed in accordance with local handling regulations.

Limitation of Liability and Payment Terms

Kensa Laboratory performs testing as an independent technical facility using recognized standard methods with EN and ASTM equivalents referenced on reports. To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, the total liability of Kensa Laboratory for any claim, error, omission, or delay arising from testing services is strictly limited to the fee paid for the specific test performed. Invoices are payable within 30 days of the invoice date, and prompt payment is required to maintain active account status.

posts.title: From Batch Plant to Final Report: Managing Concrete Specimen Verification
posts.excerpt: Understanding how concrete test specimens are prepared, cured, and mechanically crushed ensures accurate verification of structural design strength on site.
posts.content:
On any active construction site, concrete placement represents an irreversible structural commitment. Once a pour is completed, the engineering team relies on physical test specimens to confirm that the hardened material achieves its specified design strength. At Kensa Laboratory, founded in 2009 and operating from Unit 4, 18 Harbour Works Road, Northgate since 2017, our bench technicians observe daily how disciplined sample preparation directly influences test reliability. A neutral testing bench provides the essential verification that sits between the initial batch plant mix and critical structural decisions on site.

The journey of a concrete test specimen begins at the point of discharge. Fresh concrete must be sampled in strict accordance with recognized standard methods, with EN and ASTM equivalent procedures referenced on all resulting documentation. Field sampling often includes slump and air content measurements directly on site, where our mobile technicians check workability across delivered batches for $140 per visit covering up to 6 tests. Cylinders measuring 100 by 200 millimetres or 150 by 300 millimetres must be cast in rigid moulds, consolidated thoroughly, and protected from moisture loss or temperature extremes during initial setting.

Clear chain of custody is critical prior to transit. Our four-step intake procedure starts with booking a submission online, which immediately assigns a unique submission number. Every specimen must be marked with this submission number and its cast date using waterproof marker directly on the surface before dispatch. Specimens are delivered to our receiving bay, where sample reception lead Lena Hoffmann manages intake between 08:30 and 16:00 Monday through Friday. Consignments are logged within the hour of arrival, verifying specimen dimensions and condition before transfer to temperature-regulated curing tanks managed by concrete lead Tomás Ferreira.

Standard compressive strength testing evaluates sets of 3 cylinders after specified curing intervals, typically at 7 and 28 days, for a standard fee of $85 per set. In our testing hall, each cylinder is measured, weighed, and axially compressed between steel platens until ultimate failure. Our team records maximum compressive load, calculates failure stress, and logs fracture patterns. When existing structures require retrospective verification, such as our recent work on a mid-rise commercial retrofit or a pedestrian bridge deck pour, Marcus Lindqvist extracts hardened cores with diameters at least 3 times the nominal aggregate size for laboratory testing at $165 per core.

Beyond compression, our team provides comprehensive material assessment across multiple disciplines. Amara Okafor oversees rebar tensile and cold bend testing at $60 per bar to verify reinforcement ductility, while Priya Nair directs chemical chloride analysis at $95 per sample to map corrosion risks in existing concrete elements. Under the direction of lab director Ingrid Valen, all tests follow documented procedures, ensuring technical impartiality across every client project.

Once testing is complete, our laboratory issues a formal, signed PDF report within 2 working days. When projects face immediate construction deadlines or pressing pour schedules, our express service delivers verified reports within 24 hours for a 40 percent fee uplift. Tested specimens are carefully cataloged and retained in our storage facility for 30 days after reporting, providing engineers with a reliable window for additional verification. By maintaining rigorous standard procedures from intake to final reporting, independent laboratory testing provides the factual foundation structural engineers need to build with confidence.
